steps.title: Sign in to the Shopify Dev Dashboard
steps.notes: One redirect to accounts.shopify.com/lookup (with rid and verify query params). Asks for an email first, then password; also passkey, Google, Apple, Facebook, WhatsApp. No bot check or cookie banner in the screenshot. Needs a Shopify account; whether a separate developer or organization account must be set up first is not visible without signing in (UNCERTAIN). The docs only say 'You're a user with app development permissions' (verified on the live page).

steps.title: Apps > Create app > Start from Dev Dashboard > name the app > Create
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. The docs page carries a note that for an app-store app you should build with Shopify CLI instead; the Dev Dashboard path is described as the simple route for quick integrations. Only the app name is asked for at creation.

steps.title: Create a version: App URL, Webhooks API version, Scopes, then Release
steps.quote: Your app must have at least one version before it can be installed on a store
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Agent can prepare the values; a human types them into the signed-in form and clicks Release. For a non-embedded app the default App URL https://shopify.dev/apps/default-app-home is allowed. Access to protected customer data needs separate approval. Later scope changes are not auto-applied to installed stores; the merchant must approve them.

steps.title: Add Composio's callback as a redirect URL
steps.quote: Must exactly match a redirect URI you've configured in the Dev Dashboard
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page (it describes the redirect_uri parameter). Value to paste: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (per Composio docs; copy the exact value shown in your Composio auth config, since some toolkits still show the legacy v1 URL). Because Shopify requires an exact match, any difference in the value will fail at authorization time. The Dev Dashboard version form fields listed on the create-app page are App URL, Webhooks API version and Scopes only; where exactly the redirect URL field sits in the form was not seen (UNCERTAIN).

steps.title: Know the redirect URL requirement for public apps
steps.quote: You must include at least one redirect URL before making your app public
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page, but it comes from the Shopify CLI app-configuration reference (the redirect_urls setting in shopify.app.toml), not the Dev Dashboard form. The linked 'redirection URLs' rules page was not captured, so rules such as HTTPS-only, localhost, wildcards or count limits are UNCERTAIN.

steps.title: Choose the distribution method (public vs custom)
steps.quote: You can't change the distribution method after you select it
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. The table shows public distribution (many stores) has Approval required: Yes, custom distribution (one store, stores in the same Plus organization, or development stores) has Approval required: No. Where in the Dev Dashboard this choice is made was not seen (UNCERTAIN), and 'legal_acceptance' is a guess at the human reason, not seen on a page.

steps.title: For public distribution: submit the app for Shopify app review and wait
steps.quote: it goes through an app review process
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Statuses are Draft, Submitted, Reviewed, Published. Requirements are the same for fully visible and limited visibility public apps. No review time estimate was captured. Custom distribution needs no approval.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client secret from App settings into a Composio auth config
steps.quote: Copy your Client ID and Client secret
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page (from the client credentials step: select App settings, then copy). No screenshot of that part, and the real settings screen needs sign-in. Shopify's authorization code flow uses the same client ID and secret.

steps.title: At runtime each merchant is sent to a per-shop authorize URL
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page (shown in the per-user example). The screenshot crops the code block, so the full URL is only visible in docs-1-authorization-code-grant.txt. Consequence: the authorize host is the merchant's own shop domain, so the end user must supply the shop. The callback shop parameter must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\-]*\.myshopify\.com$ (verified: 'Confirm the shop parameter matches'). Docs also state 'New public apps must use expiring offline access tokens' (verified).

steps.title: App must authorize with OAuth immediately on install (App Store apps)
steps.quote: Your app should immediately authorize using OAuth before any other steps occur
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page (best-practices page that the checklist URL redirects to). It is a best practice for App Store apps, phrased as should, even if the merchant previously installed and uninstalled. Whether Composio's flow satisfies this for a public listing was not assessed.

blocked_at.what_it_asks_for: A Shopify account: email, then password, or passkey, Google, Apple, Facebook or WhatsApp sign-in.

observations: Console wall reached in one redirect, with no bot check or cookie banner.

Both docs URLs in apps.json redirected to differently named pages: the authorization-code-grant URL now lands on 'Authenticate a standalone or API-only app', and the app-requirements-checklist URL lands on 'Best practices for apps in the Shopify App Store'.
Neither of the two starting docs pages explains creating the app; the create-app steps came from the Dev Dashboard docs, and the redirect_urls rule from the CLI app-configuration reference.
14 of 14 quotes tried were found on the live pages; 10 are used in steps.json as the step quotes.
Screenshots show docs, not the real Dev Dashboard form. The real form needs a signed-in human.
